title: Did you notice this man in Titanic???
note: Charles Joughin, chief baker. Facts: Wikipedia 'Charles Joughin' (his British inquiry testimony) and 'Sinking of the Titanic'. Colour shots: Titanic (1997). Black-and-white shots: A Night to Remember (1958). Photos: public domain (Wikimedia Commons). Run from the work folder that holds src/, photos/ and tx/.

beats.say: If you pay attention, you'll notice one man in Titanic who is way too calm.
While the ship is going down, and everyone around him is screaming,
he's holding the railing right next to Jack and Rose,
and he casually takes a sip from his flask.
Most people think he's just an extra. But he was a real person.
His name was Charles Joughin, and he was the Titanic's chief baker.
beats.speak: His name was Charles Jockin, and he was the Titanic's chief baker.

beats.say: And what he did that night is even crazier than the movie.
When the ship hit the iceberg, Joughin was off duty, in his bunk.
beats.speak: When the ship hit the iceberg, Jockin was off duty, in his bunk.

beats.say: He sent his thirteen bakers up to the lifeboats, with loaves of bread.
He was even put in charge of lifeboat number ten. But he didn't get in. He helped women and children into it instead.
Then he went back down to his cabin, and had a drink. By his own account, half a glass of liqueur.
When he came back up, every lifeboat was gone. So he threw about fifty deck chairs into the sea, so people in the water would have something to float on.
Then he ran to the very back of the ship, climbed over the railing, and held on from the outside.
Exactly where Jack and Rose are in the movie.
When the stern finally went down, he said he rode it like an elevator. His head barely got wet.
That made him the last survivor to leave the Titanic.
And the water he landed in? Jack describes it perfectly.
Almost everyone who ended up in that water died within minutes.
But Joughin claimed he stayed in it for about two hours, and said he hardly felt the cold.
beats.speak: But Jockin claimed he stayed in it for about two hours, and said he hardly felt the cold.

beats.say: He believed it was the alcohol. Historians still argue about it.
At dawn, he reached an overturned lifeboat. There was no room for him, so a cook who knew him held his hand, while his legs stayed in the water.
Another lifeboat picked him up, and the rescue ship Carpathia took him in, with nothing worse than swollen feet.
He lived until 1956.
So next time you watch Titanic, look for the calm man with the flask.
